name: Chennai
shortDescription: Tamil Nadu's coastal capital brings together temple traditions, classical arts, long urban beaches, colonial history and one of South India's richest food cultures.
description:
Chennai is often treated as a gateway, but the city itself deserves time. Mylapore's temple streets, the museums and churches of the colonial centre, Kalakshetra's classical-arts legacy and the Bay of Bengal waterfront reveal different layers of the former Madras.

Plan by corridor rather than distance. Combine Mylapore and San Thome, keep Fort St George with George Town, and treat DakshinaChitra or Mahabalipuram as a separate southern excursion. The Metro and suburban rail help on selected routes, but autos and app cabs still cover many final connections.

Heat and humidity shape every itinerary. Begin outdoor visits early, schedule a long midday break and approach the sea responsibly: Chennai's beaches are valued gathering spaces, but currents can be dangerous and swimming is not automatically safe.
bestTimeToVisit:
November to February is the most comfortable period for walking, performances and day trips, though humidity remains. December and January coincide with Chennai's major classical music and dance season.

March to June is very hot; outdoor plans need early starts. The northeast monsoon, especially October to December, can bring intense rain and urban flooding. Check weather and transport alerts rather than assuming ordinary monsoon patterns elsewhere in India apply here.
bestTimeToVisitShort: November to February; monitor northeast-monsoon rain
budgetEstimate: ₹1,800–6,000 per person per day (excluding intercity travel)

topAttractions.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
topAttractions.description: Mylapore's active Shiva temple is known for its colourful gopuram and ritual life. Dress modestly, leave shoes outside and respect areas restricted to worshippers.
topAttractions.timings: Temple schedule includes midday closure; verify locally

topAttractions.name: Marina Beach
topAttractions.description: The broad Bay of Bengal waterfront is central to Chennai's public life, especially around sunrise and evening. Enjoy the promenade but follow warnings about strong currents.
topAttractions.timings: Open public space; visit in cooler hours

topAttractions.name: Government Museum, Egmore
topAttractions.description: A major museum complex with archaeology, bronze sculpture, natural history and art collections. Check which galleries are open before allocating a full afternoon.
topAttractions.timings: Usually closed Friday and public holidays; verify

topAttractions.name: Fort St George
topAttractions.description: The East India Company's seventeenth-century base now contains government offices, St Mary's Church and a museum that explains colonial Madras.

topAttractions.name: San Thome Basilica
topAttractions.description: A prominent neo-Gothic Catholic basilica in Mylapore associated with the tradition of St Thomas. Visit quietly outside services.

topAttractions.name: DakshinaChitra
topAttractions.description: A living museum south of the city presenting regional houses, crafts and performance traditions from southern India. Allow several hours and combine it with the ECR corridor.
topAttractions.timings: Verify weekly closure and programme schedule

topAttractions.name: Kalakshetra Foundation
topAttractions.description: A landmark institution for Bharatanatyam, music and traditional arts in a leafy campus. General access and performances require checking in advance.

topAttractions.name: Guindy National Park
topAttractions.description: A protected urban ecosystem with dry evergreen vegetation and wildlife in the city's south. Visitor access is more structured than an ordinary public park.

localFood.name: Idli, Dosa and Filter Coffee
localFood.description: Chennai's classic tiffin combination ranges from soft idli to crisp dosa, with sambar, chutneys and strong metal-tumbler coffee.
localFood.whereToTry: Established vegetarian restaurants in Mylapore, Triplicane and T Nagar

localFood.name: Tamil Meals
localFood.description: Rice served with sambar, rasam, vegetables, curd and changing accompaniments offers the broadest introduction to everyday Tamil cooking.

localFood.name: Kothu Parotta
localFood.description: Chopped flaky parotta stir-fried on a hot griddle with egg, vegetables or meat and an audible rhythm of metal spatulas.

localFood.name: Chettinad Dishes
localFood.description: Pepper, aromatics and roasted spices define many dishes associated with the Chettinad region, including vegetarian and meat preparations.

localFood.name: Sundal
localFood.description: Seasoned legumes with coconut and spices make a light beach or festival snack.
localFood.whereToTry: Reputable beach vendors and snack shops

localFood.name: Jigarthanda
localFood.description: A chilled Madurai-origin drink of milk, syrup and almond gum that has become popular across Chennai.
localFood.whereToTry: Established South Tamil Nadu sweet and drink shops

tips: Use Metro or suburban rail when they align with your route, then autos for the last mile.
Insist on a meter or app-confirmed auto fare.
Keep East Coast Road attractions on a separate day from central Chennai.
Start outdoor sightseeing early and take a midday heat break.
Monitor heavy-rain alerts during the northeast monsoon.
Do not swim where beach warnings or currents make conditions unsafe.
Dress modestly and follow access rules at active temples.
Check December performance tickets early during the music season.
Choose busy food shops and drink filtered or sealed water.
Mylapore suits culture and traditional food.
Egmore offers rail and museum access.
T Nagar suits shopping but is congested.
ECR works for coastal resorts, not a central-city itinerary.

hiddenGems: Theosophical Society surroundings - A historic, green part of Adyar whose internal access can be limited; verify before visiting.
Cholamandal Artists' Village - A pioneering artists' community and gallery campus on the East Coast Road.
Kasimedu Fishing Harbour - A working harbour best approached early with a responsible guide and respect for workers.
Armenian Church - A quiet eighteenth-century church in George Town with limited visiting arrangements.
Broken Bridge viewpoints - Coastal views near the Adyar estuary; access and safety conditions vary, so do not visit isolated stretches alone.
Pulicat Lake - A brackish-water landscape north of Chennai suited to a planned seasonal birding excursion.

faq.question: How many days are enough for Chennai?
faq.answer: Two days cover Mylapore, the waterfront and central museums; three allows DakshinaChitra or a focused arts experience.

faq.question: Is Marina Beach safe for swimming?
faq.answer: Do not assume so. Strong currents occur, and visitors should follow lifeguard and local safety warnings.

faq.question: What is special about December in Chennai?
faq.answer: The city hosts a major season of Carnatic music and Bharatanatyam performances, with popular events requiring advance planning.

faq.question: Can Mahabalipuram be a day trip?
faq.answer: Yes. It lies south along the East Coast Road and works best as a dedicated day rather than being combined with central sights.
